issues.description: Inconsistent zero-value discipline: File uses nil-receiver checks while sibling types use IsZero()
issues.detail: The patch establishes two different conventions for the same problem. *File methods guard with `if f == nil`, while Type, Member, Oneof, etc. guard with `if x.IsZero()`. There is no stated invariant explaining why the receiver-nilness predicate differs across the package. A reader cannot derive, from the code alone, which predicate to use when adding the next accessor. This is precisely the accreted complexity that structured discipline is meant to prevent. Pick one definition of 'zero' per type kind and state it as the precondition for every accessor.

issues.description: Reflection-driven test is TESTED-NOT-PROVED for the property it claims to establish
issues.detail: TestZero iterates `ty.NumMethod()` and calls every nullary method, asserting that returns are zero. This establishes a property over the methods that exist today, not over the contract 'every accessor on a zero value returns a zero value and does not panic.' Methods added later are silently included with no specification check; methods with non-nullary signatures (the very ones most likely to dereference an unchecked field) are silently excluded. The test cannot distinguish 'this method was written correctly' from 'this method happens not to dereference anything on this particular zero layout.' Testing shows the presence of bugs, not their absence; the postcondition is not implied by the test passing.

issues.description: Defensive-as-substitute: nil and zero guards replace a missing type invariant
issues.detail: Across ir_file.go, ir_imports.go, ir_member.go, ir_type.go, ir_value.go, dozens of accessors now begin with `if f == nil` / `if x.IsZero()` returning a hand-rolled zero. This is defensive programming used in place of a stated invariant on the constructor of these types. Either the zero value is a valid inhabitant of the type (in which case the invariant should be documented once and the accessors should not need to know), or it is not (in which case calling accessors on it is a precondition violation and the guards are masking a bug at the call site). The patch does neither; it adds N independent guards, each of which must be remembered for every future accessor. This is the unstructured-control-flow problem one level up: a smuggled disjunction in every method.

issues.description: Special case in ValueNodeIndex (-1 sentinel) introduced without specification update at callers
issues.detail: Element.ValueNodeIndex now returns -1 for the zero value, and the doc comment notes 'If the element is empty, this returns -1.' The example in the same doc comment, `key := e.Value().MessageKeys().At(e.ValueNodeIndex())`, will index with -1 on a zero element, which is presumably a panic at the next step. The postcondition has been weakened without any audit of the call sites that consume this return. Either document that callers must check the result, or have those callers check IsZero themselves and keep the function's postcondition tight.

issues.description: Test special-cases IsZero, ValueNodeIndex, and Context inline rather than via a per-type specification
issues.detail: The switch in testZeroAny on method name encodes the specification 'IsZero returns true, ValueNodeIndex returns -1, Context returns a *ir.File' as a name-matching block. New exceptions will accrete here. A cleaner discipline would name the per-type postcondition as data (a table of expected sentinel returns per method per type) and have the loop verify against that table; the asymmetry between 'most methods return zero' and 'these three return something else' should be expressed in the specification, not buried in a switch in the harness.

issues.description: imports.Transitive comment/code mismatch persists under the new guard
issues.detail: The slice `i.files[:max(0, len(i.files)-1)]` is annotated 'Exclude the implicit descriptor.proto.' but for a non-nil imports with zero files, max(0, -1) yields 0 and nothing is excluded because nothing exists; for one file, it excludes that one file regardless of whether it is descriptor.proto. The invariant 'the last element of i.files is the implicit descriptor.proto' is load-bearing and undocumented at the type. The new nil guard does not fix this; it merely makes the existing latent assumption survive a nil receiver. Document the invariant on `imports.files` or the unconditional drop-last is unreasoned.

review.summary: The patch makes the IR package's accessors total over the zero value, which is a defensible goal, but it does so by sprinkling per-method guards (sometimes `f == nil`, sometimes `IsZero()`) rather than by stating a type-level invariant about what a zero value is and what its accessors return. The result is DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE: dozens of independent local checks standing in for one specification. The accompanying test is TESTED-NOT-PROVED — a reflection sweep over currently-existing nullary methods cannot establish the postcondition 'all accessors on a zero value return zero values and do not panic,' only that today's particular set happens to. Element.ValueNodeIndex's new -1 sentinel weakens a postcondition without auditing call sites. Verdict: useful work, but the discipline is wrong; refactor toward a stated zero-value contract per type, then make the test verify that contract from a per-type table rather than from method-name string matching.
